jurisdictions.framework: LGPD (Lei Geral de Proteção de Dados)
jurisdictions.territorial_scope: Applies to any processing of personal data in Brazil, including data processed by foreign entities if the data is accessed or used in Brazil. Applies to payment flows where users are Brazilian residents or transactions occur within Brazil.
lawful_bases: Legitimate interest (only for fraud detection with strict safeguards)
cross_border_transfers: Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) approved by ANPD
Data localization: All personal data must be stored in Brazil; no transfers to foreign servers without prior authorization from ANPD.

data_subject_rights.right_to_access: Within 10 business days of request; may be extended by up to 5 days with justification.
data_subject_rights.right_to_correction: Within 10 business days; must be fulfilled if data is inaccurate or incomplete.
data_subject_rights.right_to_erasure: Within 10 business days; exceptions apply for legal obligations, public interest, or financial records.
data_subject_rights.financial_records_exception: Financial records may not be erased under LGPD; must remain accessible for tax and audit purposes.

breach_notification.timeline: Report to ANPD within 72 hours of discovery

registration_obligations: Mandatory appointment of a local representative in Brazil for any data processing activity involving personal data.
Submission of data processing inventory to ANPD within 30 days of launch.
conflicts_with_group_program: Group's cookie consent manager is not designed for mobile or payment flows; requires re-architecture.
Group's records-of-processing inventory does not support data localization requirements; must be updated with storage location and access controls.
No local representative appointed in the group program — requires new appointment.

jurisdictions.territorial_scope: Applies to any processing of personal data in Kenya, including data processed by foreign entities if accessed or used in Kenya. Applies to payment flows where users are Kenyan residents or transactions occur within Kenya.
lawful_bases: Legitimate interest (only for fraud detection with strict safeguards)
cross_border_transfers: Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) approved by NDPA
Data localization: All personal data must be stored in Kenya; no transfers to foreign servers without prior authorization from NDPA.

data_subject_rights.right_to_access: Within 30 days of request; may be extended with justification.
data_subject_rights.right_to_erasure: Within 30 days of request; exceptions apply for legal obligations or financial records.
data_subject_rights.financial_records_exception: Financial records must remain accessible for tax and audit purposes.

breach_notification.timeline: Report to NDPA within 72 hours of discovery

registration_obligations: Mandatory appointment of a local representative in Kenya for any data processing activity involving personal data.
Submission of data processing inventory to NDPA within 30 days of launch.
conflicts_with_group_program: Group's consent manager is not designed for mobile or payment flows; requires re-architecture.
No local representative appointed in the group program — requires new appointment.
PDPA allows longer response windows than LGPD, but still requires faster action than group standard.

jurisdictions.territorial_scope: Applies to any processing of personal data in Poland, including data processed by foreign entities if accessed or used in Poland. Applies to payment flows where users are Polish residents or transactions occur within Poland.
lawful_bases: Legitimate interest (only for fraud detection with strict safeguards)
cross_border_transfers: Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) approved by Polish Data Protection Authority
Data localization: Not required under GDPR; data may be transferred to EU-based servers.

data_subject_rights.right_to_access: Within 30 days of request; may be extended with justification.
data_subject_rights.right_to_erasure: Within 30 days of request; exceptions apply for legal obligations or financial records.
data_subject_rights.financial_records_exception: Financial records must remain accessible for tax and audit purposes.

breach_notification.timeline: Report to UOKiK within 72 hours of discovery

registration_obligations: Mandatory appointment of a local representative in Poland for any data processing activity involving personal data.
Submission of data processing inventory to UOKiK within 30 days of launch.
conflicts_with_group_program: Group's consent manager is not designed for payment flows; requires extension or re-architecture.
GDPR allows SCCs without local representative, but requires explicit documentation and approval — group program lacks this.
No local representative appointed in the group program — requires new appointment.

cross_jurisdictional_conflicts.description: Brazil and Kenya require data to be stored locally; Poland does not. This creates a conflict between Brazil/Kenya and the group's existing infrastructure, which is currently hosted in Europe.
cross_jurisdictional_conflicts.impact: Requires engineering redesign of data flow or use of local servers in Brazil and Kenya; cannot rely on current EU-based processing.

cross_jurisdictional_conflicts.description: All three jurisdictions require a local representative for data processing activities, but the group program currently lacks this structure.
cross_jurisdictional_conflicts.impact: Must appoint distinct local representatives per market or establish a regional one — open decision with significant legal and operational implications.

cross_jurisdictional_conflicts.description: Brazil requires faster response windows (10 days) than Kenya (30 days), which in turn is slower than Poland's 30-day window. This creates inconsistency in how the group handles data access and correction requests.
cross_jurisdictional_conflicts.impact: Requires a unified process with tiered handling or market-specific workflows to meet minimum requirements.

cross_jurisdictional_conflicts.description: All three jurisdictions require breach reporting within 72 hours, but Brazil's ANPD may impose additional enforcement actions if not reported promptly.
cross_jurisdictional_conflicts.impact: Must ensure a single, unified incident response system with real-time monitoring and automated alerts.

likelihood_impact_scale.low: Unlikely to occur and has minimal impact on operations; typically requires no action beyond monitoring.
likelihood_impact_scale.medium: Moderate likelihood of occurrence with moderate impact; requires proactive mitigation and monitoring.
likelihood_impact_scale.high: High probability of occurrence with significant operational or reputational consequences; requires immediate action and escalation.

risks.title: Local regulator changes guidance mid-program
risks.mitigation: Maintain a real-time monitoring dashboard with local regulators; establish quarterly review cycles to track policy shifts. Update compliance plans within 72 hours of any guidance change.
risks.early_warning_indicator: Public announcement or press release from ANPD, NDPA, or UOKiK regarding new data processing rules.

risks.title: Third-party processor failure in-market
risks.mitigation: Implement failover mechanisms and data redundancy at the regional level. Maintain a list of approved backup processors with pre-approved SCCs.
risks.early_warning_indicator: Service outage or latency spike in payment flows reported by users or monitoring tools.

risks.title: Failure to meet breach notification timelines
risks.mitigation: Deploy real-time anomaly detection and automated alerting. Establish a 24/7 incident response team with direct access to local authorities.
risks.early_warning_indicator: Unscheduled breach event detected in monitoring systems.

risks.title: Data localization failure due to technical constraints
risks.mitigation: Design data flows with fallbacks to regional servers. Conduct stress testing under real-world load conditions.
risks.early_warning_indicator: Performance degradation or unavailability in Brazil/Kenya payment flows.

risks.title: Inadequate consent handling for fraud detection
risks.mitigation: Implement dynamic, time-bound consent with clear user opt-in paths. Document all use cases and provide transparency to users.
risks.early_warning_indicator: User complaints or support tickets related to fraud detection actions.

risks.title: Non-compliant third-party vendor due diligence
risks.mitigation: Require all vendors to complete updated questionnaires with jurisdiction-specific clauses. Conduct annual audits.
risks.early_warning_indicator: Vendor audit failure or non-compliance notice.

risks.title: Failure to appoint local representative in time for launch
risks.mitigation: Finalize appointment strategy at Phase 0; assign a dedicated legal lead per market with clear timelines.
risks.early_warning_indicator: Delay in local counsel confirmation or registration submission.

risks.title: Data subject rights response delays
risks.mitigation: Automate access and correction requests with real-time routing to support teams.
risks.early_warning_indicator: High volume of data subject rights requests within a short period.

risks.title: Inconsistent handling of financial records across jurisdictions
risks.mitigation: Establish a centralized policy for financial record retention with jurisdiction-specific exceptions.
risks.early_warning_indicator: Discrepancies in data access or erasure requests involving financial records.

risks.title: Lack of cross-border transfer mechanism approval
risks.mitigation: Ensure all SCCs are pre-approved by local authorities before deployment.
risks.early_warning_indicator: Failure to receive approval from ANPD, NDPA, or UOKiK for data transfer.

risks.title: Insufficient staff training on new compliance requirements
risks.mitigation: Develop jurisdiction-specific training modules and conduct mandatory sessions before launch.
risks.early_warning_indicator: Increased support tickets or user complaints related to data handling.

risks.title: Group program fails to integrate with existing infrastructure
risks.mitigation: Conduct integration testing early in Phase 0; use sandbox environments for all compliance features.
risks.early_warning_indicator: System errors or data loss during test runs.

open_decisions.decision_title: Appointment of local representatives in each market
open_decisions.proposed_option_a: Appoint a distinct local representative per market (Brazil, Kenya, Poland)
open_decisions.proposed_option_b: Appoint a single regional representative overseeing all three markets
open_decisions.justification: Brazil and Kenya require data localization; Poland does not. A single regional representative may lack authority to enforce local rules under LGPD/PDPA.
open_decisions.escalation_path: Escalate to Legal - Global Compliance (Head of Legal) and CIO for final approval within 14 days.

open_decisions.decision_title: Consent architecture extension or fork per market
open_decisions.proposed_option_a: Extend the group consent manager to support payment flows with dynamic consent logic
open_decisions.proposed_option_b: Fork a market-specific consent architecture (Brazil, Kenya, Poland) with separate flows and UIs
open_decisions.justification: Payment flows require different user journeys; fraud detection uses legitimate interest basis under LGPD/PDPA/GDPR.
open_decisions.escalation_path: Escalate to Product Management and Legal - Global Compliance for joint review within 14 days.

constraints: No additional headcount beyond two analyst requisitions already approved.
Launch windows are fixed: Brazil (2025-03-09), Kenya (2025-06-08), Poland (2025-09-07).
Any workstream that cannot complete before its market's launch must carry a documented compensating control.
